definition: persistently demanding to the point of annoyance
memoryTip: Im-portune: keep asking until it’s annoying.
correctPassage: Importunate callers continued to press for an early decision.
wrongPassages: They hoped to importunate the protest by moving the hearing to a smaller room.
She hoped to importunate the injury by returning to full practice the next morning.
They tried to importunate the landslide by calling the slope “historically quiet.”

definition: skill in performing tasks, especially with the hands
memoryTip: Dexterous hands — skilled handling.
correctPassage: Repairing the mechanism required considerable manual dexterity.
wrongPassages: She filed absence reason dexterity and attached a blank PDF.
He laminated a card that said Dexterity Point with an arrow to nowhere.
The foam dexterity cutout became a phone stand on the workbench.

definition: without regard to; regardless of
memoryTip: Ir-respective: without respect to X — regardless.
correctPassage: The rule applies to all students, irrespective of major.
wrongPassages: The lobby’s irrespective plants leaned toward a painted sun on the wall.
Managers announced an irrespective freeze that still allowed executive bonuses.
His irrespective subpoena schedule listed files already produced in discovery.

definition: excessive pride in appearance or achievements
memoryTip: Vain about looks/status — excessive pride.
correctPassage: The project was driven more by vanity than by public need.
wrongPassages: The release notes listed a vanity of “bug fixes” without naming any bug.
In the lab notebook, “vanity” was written as the sample’s mass in milligrams.
He stored stove fuel under the label vanity by mistake.

definition: not transparent; hard to understand
memoryTip: Can’t see through — unclear meaning too.
correctPassage: The process remains opaque to anyone outside the committee.
wrongPassages: Her opaque bibliography pointed to pages that did not exist.
His opaque half-title thanked a series editor who was never hired.
Her opaque order to show cause omitted the hearing date entirely.

definition: many and of various types
memoryTip: Multi + farious forms — many varied kinds.
correctPassage: Her multifarious interests range from botany to experimental music.
wrongPassages: She closed planning as multifarious with half the scope still marked TBD.
The station’s multifarious platform screen showed the previous day’s departures.
Fans called the Atmos mix multifarious for pushing dialogue into the rear channels only.

definition: arranged in layers; divided into status levels
memoryTip: In strata (layers) — stacked levels of status or rock.
correctPassage: Access to care is stratified by income and geography.
wrongPassages: Listeners found the lecture stratified because no term was left undefined on the board.
Councils axed the stratified crossing-guard hours parents had requested.
The break stud was stratified: intact past any design shear load.

definition: having real importance or firm basis
memoryTip: Has substance — real and important, not fluff.
correctPassage: The board asked for substantive changes, not cosmetic edits.
wrongPassages: The safety valve was substantive and never lifted in the pressure test.
Viewers found the IMAX remaster substantive for stretching 4:3 into empty side panels.
He set all services to substantive while half still showed climbing errors.

definition: a long step; or progress made
memoryTip: Long step — or progress (“made strides”).
correctPassage: Public health has made a significant stride against the disease.
wrongPassages: The writ was stride: caption, parties, and a short prayer for relief.
The coda was stride: it opened a new theme instead of closing the old one.
The pier’s stride life-ring cabinet held only an empty hook.

definition: proceeding gradually and subtly with harmful effects
memoryTip: In-side-ious: sneaks in harmfully from inside.
correctPassage: An insidious form of bias can creep into even careful studies.
wrongPassages: The plan looked insidious on paper: every risk already removed and every owner named.
Engineers left the bridge insidious after inspectors cleared heavier trucks than before.
The sample stayed insidious under heat and pressure that ruined every other trial.

definition: bring oneself into favor through flattery
memoryTip: In-grace: flattery to get into someone’s good graces.
correctPassage: He tried to ingratiate himself with the new director through constant flattery.
wrongPassages: Coaches tried to ingratiate fitness with a drill everyone already performed perfectly.
He tried to ingratiate the audit by deleting the folder auditors had requested.
The monitor will ingratiate pages by requiring three human approvals to page anyone.

definition: excessively talkative about trivial matters
memoryTip: Garble of endless talk — too chatty.
correctPassage: A garrulous seatmate made the long flight feel even longer.
wrongPassages: The bergschrund edge felt garrulous on a summer bridge with handrails.
The mix was garrulous after every track was balanced to the same loudness.
The storm left the town garrulous by restoring power before anyone noticed a flicker.

definition: intensely enthusiastic or passionate
memoryTip: Fervor on fire — intensely passionate.
correctPassage: Fervid supporters filled the square hours before the speech.
wrongPassages: The shear bolt was fervid: it held past the gearbox’s design torque.
The atrium’s fervid planting was one species set in a rigid grid.
The waterfront looked fervid when cranes, ferries, and markets all ran at once.

definition: pressing; demanding immediate attention
memoryTip: Exigent emergency — demands immediate attention.
correctPassage: Exigent circumstances justified the emergency order.
wrongPassages: The freeze made the lake exigent—thick enough for trucks to cross safely.
Traders wanted exigent news so prices would gap overnight.
The center hoped to exigent FCR by forbidding any second-contact code.

definition: understood by only a small specialist group
memoryTip: Eso-teric: inner circle only — specialist knowledge.
correctPassage: The seminar covers esoteric topics rarely taught to undergraduates.
wrongPassages: The carr pool stayed esoteric after the beck was piped away underground.
The playa lake stayed esoteric in a file with no precipitation at all.
an esoteric interface shows one button and hides every setting.

definition: drain of energy; weaken
memoryTip: E-nerve-ate: take the nerves/energy out — weaken (not energize!).
correctPassage: Heat and humidity can enervate even seasoned hikers.
wrongPassages: The station’s enervate wayfinding used icons no traveler recognized.
She closed planning as enervate with scope still listed as TBD.
The coal staith looked enervate with conveyors rusted into place.

definition: hostile and aggressive
memoryTip: Belli-gerent: war-making; aggressive.
correctPassage: A belligerent tone in the letter made negotiation unlikely.
wrongPassages: The fusible plug was belligerent and stayed intact past melt temperature.
The packet stand looked belligerent between sailings with gates shut.
Her belligerent notes filled two binders with an index and full cross-references.

definition: wanting or devouring great quantities
memoryTip: Vora = devour — huge appetite for food or books.
correctPassage: A voracious reader, she finished several novels each week.
wrongPassages: The tonic drone was voracious under a coda that never returned home.
The coastline stayed voracious in models that froze sea level forever.
The floodway stayed voracious in plans that forbade new construction.

definition: a change of circumstances, often unwelcome
memoryTip: Vici-change: ups and downs of fortune.
correctPassage: The firm survived every vicissitude of the market cycle.
wrongPassages: The hub’s vicissitude map was last updated two renovations ago.
The fen pool stayed vicissitude when the catchwater ditch ran dry.
The courtyard’s vicissitude design repeated one tile without any variation.

definition: looking or sounding sad and dismal
memoryTip: Lugubrious funeral face — exaggeratedly mournful.
correctPassage: A lugubrious soundtrack made the short film feel longer than it was.
wrongPassages: After the numbered checklist, the instructions no longer felt lugubrious to anyone on the team.
The courtyard’s lugubrious fountain never recirculated any water.
a lugubrious cron job prints “alive” and then exits.
